muller.kick: Earliest angiosperm pollen · Hughes, McDougall & Chapman 1991
muller.region: English Wealden, Kingsclere borehole KCE 777 (preparation Y391; stubs AM592, AM593); ten specimens
muller.full: Hughes, N. F., A. B. McDougall and J. L. Chapman. 1991. Exceptional new record of Cretaceous Hauterivian angiospermid pollen from southern England. Journal of Micropalaeontology 10: 75-82.
muller.note: The authors call it the earliest pollen with generally accepted angiospermid characters. The same palaeotaxon is the single Warlingham grain WM 1488/7 that Hughes figured in 1977 (Wealden grain A here). They found no precursors in older Hauterivian or Valanginian rocks of Britain, and note that Trevisan's (1988) Valanginian-Hauterivian grains from Italy have simple, unsegmented muri
muller.basis: drawn from photos of the fossil: Plates 1-3 (SEM). monosulcate, coarse reticulum of sharply segmented muri on sturdy (bottle-shaped) columellae; the tectum breaks into small mural fragments over the aperture; isolated baculae in some lumina (specimen C); size estimated from the 10 micron scale bars (check)
muller.cite: Hughes, N. F., A. B. McDougall and J. L. Chapman. 1991. Exceptional new record of Cretaceous Hauterivian angiospermid pollen from southern England. Journal of Micropalaeontology 10: 75-82. Plates 1-3.
